reports.title: Axon reports record Q3 2026 revenue of $909 million, up 28% year over year

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: •Revenue: We expect revenue of $990 million to $1.01 billion.
•Adjusted EBITDA: We expect Adjusted EBITDA of $245 million to $250 million.

◦We provide Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance, rather than net income margin guidance, due to the inherent difficulty of forecasting certain types of expenses and gains such as stock-based compensation, income tax expenses and gains or losses on marketable securities and strategic investments, which affect net income but not Adjusted EBITDA. We are unable to reasonably estimate the impact of such expenses, which could be material, on net income. Accordingly, we do not provide forward-looking reconciliations of these measures.

desk.headline: Revenue up 28% to $909m, below estimates; adjusted EPS $1.72 missed; 2026 growth outlook cut to ~30%
results: Revenue rose 28% to a record $909m but came in below the $934m estimate; adjusted EPS of $1.72 missed the $1.89 estimate.
Software & Services grew 43% to $437m; Connected Devices grew 16%, held back by a delayed ~$30m federal counter-drone (Dedrone) deployment.
Adjusted gross margin fell to 59.2% from 62.7% on more counter-drone hardware and higher memory-chip costs, but adjusted EBITDA still rose 33%.
Free cash flow was -$19m after about $100m was put into extra inventory to protect supply.
Axon is investing $1.2bn more in drone maker Skydio, taking its stake to 37% and becoming its exclusive public-safety distributor in the US and Canada.

guidance.summary: Axon cut its 2026 revenue growth outlook to about 30% (was 32-34%) after removing about $130m of delayed federal counter-drone deals, and lowered its free cash flow target. Q4 revenue is guided at $990m-1.01bn, below what analysts expected.

points: Management framed the shortfall as timing: three large federal counter-drone deals slipped on procurement cycles and integration logistics, not lost demand.
CEO Rick Smith called drones a foundational technology for the next decade, backing the Skydio stake.
Newer software (real-time operations, records, AI, 911, Dedrone software) is near a $500m annual run rate; AI recurring revenue passed $100m.
Higher memory-chip costs are expected to weigh on margins into 2027 and 2028.
The inventory build should ease after Q1 2027, which management expects to lift cash flow back up.
call.source: Shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1); StockStory call review (6 Nov 2026)
